This page discusses the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore's (MPA) cybersecurity tabletop exercises aimed at improving port resilience through business continuity planning. The exercises involve international participants and simulate cyberattacks across multiple ports, testing coordination mechanisms under different regulatory frameworks. It emphasizes the importance of considering cyber risks alongside physical risks and suggests backup strategies for recovery.

This page discusses the enforcement and oversight of cybersecurity regulations in ports, highlighting various national frameworks and their implementation. It emphasizes the differences in institutional capacity and regulatory maturity across countries, with examples from Japan, Singapore, and the EU. The text also notes the uneven development of cybersecurity governance, with statistics on countries having national strategies and agencies, and the impact of legal instruments on compliance and enforcement.
